bilingualEducationNotes: Some curriculum areas are taught in Maya, Garifuna or Xinka and others in Spanish
The first language for learning is each pupil's mother tongue and the second another national
The national education system must use Maya, Garifuna and Xinka at every level
Where Maya, Garifuna or Xinka monolingualism predominates teaching is in the pupils' language
Bilingualism in national languages is compulsory for public and private sector pupils

sources.label: Ley de Idiomas Nacionales, Decreto Número 19-2003, artículo 13, y su Reglamento, Acuerdo Gubernativo Número 320-2011, artículos 7 y 8 (compilation hosted by Municipalidad de Tejutla)
Modelo Educativo Bilingüe e Intercultural, MINEDUC/DIGEBI, quoting Acuerdo Gubernativo 22-2004 artículos 1 y 2

bilingualEducationNotes: Indigenous languages are used in the official and private schools of the comarcas
The recognised languages are Ngäbe, Buglé, Kuna, Emberá, Wounaan, Naso Tjerdi and Bri Bri
A gradual and staged process carries it through all levels and modalities
Implementation is obligatory in official and private schools in all indigenous communities
The implementation plan is to reach more than 132,000 children and young people

l1Support: Heritage Language is one of the accepted ESL service models an LEA may use
Many structured English immersion programmes provide bilingual support
An LEA may decide to assess a pupil in the native language on a case-by-case basis
Notifications to parents must be translated into a language the parents can understand
A bilingual published paper dictionary is listed among EL testing accommodations
